newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PRESIDENT SIGNS RELAXED ABORTION BILL.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PRESIDENT SIGNS RELAXED ABORTION BILL.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Wednesday signed into law a bill relaxing the country's strict anti-abortion rules, the president's spokesman said.
The bill, strongly opposed by the powerful Roman Catholic church, allows for the abortion when women are in a difficult personal or financial situation.
"The president signed the bill on family planning and protection of the foetus and conditions for termination of pregnancy," Antoni Styrczula told Reuters.

The new law, condemned by Polish-born Pope John Paul II, was pushed through parliament by the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) party in defiance of pro-church rightist opposition.
The measure allows women to end pregnancies before the 12th week but only after counselling and a period of reflection and provides sex education in schools and cheaper contraception.

Under the previous law, passed in 1993 by a pro-Catholic government, abortions were allowed only if a pregnancy threatened a woman's life or health, resulted from incest or rape, or when the foetus was irreparably damaged. Doctors who violated the law faced up to two years in prison.
